data.one_liner: Lightweight reactive framework with observable values, lists, sets, maps, and event emitters.
data.what_it_does: Provides non-intrusive reactive primitives like RxValue, RxList, RxSet, RxMap, and Emitter that use Dart Streams to update UI automatically when data changes.
use_when: You want lightweight, stream-backed observables without code generation.
You prefer separating models from their reactive wrappers.
You need reactive collections (lists, sets, maps) with conditional add helpers.
avoid_when: You want a fully-fledged architecture pattern like BLoC or Redux.
You rely heavily on widget-tree based state inheritance like Provider or Riverpod.
strengths: Supports reactive values, lists, sets, maps, and event emitters out of the box.
weaknesses: Lacks built-in dependency injection compared to comprehensive state solutions.
Requires manual plumbing to connect observables to the UI tree.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a more robust, compile-safe dependency injection and state management solution for Flutter.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers a strict, predictable event-driven state management pattern suitable for large applications.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers simpler widget-tree scoped state inheritance.
